dish: Yushi-dōfu soba (limited, with tofu from Nanjō's Hanashiro Kiyo Tōfu-ten) and tonkotsu-dashi soba with homemade curly noodles
n: Okinawa Soba Kōganeya, Haebaru (沖縄そば こがね家)
w: A Haebaru soba specialist opened in September 2024 by local-born owner Higa Tatsuhiro, serving a rich pork-bone broth finished with bonito over homemade curly noodles. Ryukyu Shimpo covered its limited yushi-dōfu soba (¥900) made with tofu from a long-running traditional Nanjō tofu maker, and Okinawa Times reported the shop 'thriving' on simple flavour with locals coming daily.

dish: Nankotsu-soki soba (soft-bone pork rib) in a choice of assari or kotteri broth; chicken-cutlet soba
w: A Yonabaru soba house founded in 1985, serving homemade noodles in two broths — a light pork/chicken/bonito/kombu soup and a rich multi-bone one — with nankotsu-soki soba the most popular bowl. It was one of eight southern shops chosen in Okinawa Times' 2023 poll of 900 noodle lovers, and also ranks in an ITmedia Netorabo reader poll of Okinawa soba.

dish: Shirokuma ('white bear') shaved ice — a kintoki kakigōri shaped as a bear's face with red-bean eyes
n: Inamine Hiyashimono Senmon Oshokujidokoro, Itoman (いなみね冷し物専門 お食事処)
w: A long-running Itoman cold-sweets and set-meal shop (31 years per OCVB's Itoman listing) famous for its shirokuma — a mound of kintoki shaved ice decorated as a bear's face — alongside Okinawa soba and champurū set meals. Rurubu lists it as a signature Itoman sweets stop and Taiwan's TVBS SuperTaste featured it.

dish: Nepalese curries made with Okinawan vegetables — Karika Special set, spinach-chicken and mutton curry, with chai or lassi
n: Shokudō Karika, Mibaru Beach, Nanjō (食堂かりか)
address: Mibaru Beach, Hyakuna, Tamagusuku, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan
w: An open-air beach restaurant on Mibaru Beach where a Nepalese chef cooks curries with local Okinawan vegetables; diners order at the window and eat at tables set on the sand by the waves. Cotrip and GLTJP (Good Luck Trip) both feature it among Nanjō's ocean-front eats.

dish: Umibudō (sea-grape) soft serve mixed with morning-picked sea grapes; sea-grape picking and Okinawa soba at the farm's own restaurant
n: Umibudō Farm Umin-chi, Itoman (海ぶどう農園 海ん道)
w: A working sea-grape (umibudō) farm on the Itoman coast with a shop, its own Okinawa soba restaurant and picking experiences; its signature is soft serve folded with fresh-picked sea grapes. Ryukyu Shimpo reported on the farm and OCVB's official Itoman–Tomigusuku 'fishermen's-town gourmet' course includes it as a stop.

dish: Bakudan onigiri — Itoman's fishermen's rice ball wrapped in round kamaboko fish-cake; sugar-cane soft serve
n: Itoman Ichiba Itomāru, Itoman (糸満市場いとま～る)
address: Itoman, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan (near Itoman fishing port)
w: Itoman's long-running town market (machigwā), rebuilt in 2020 with about 28 indoor stalls — fishmongers, butchers and kamaboko makers alongside new cafés — where you can try the bakudan onigiri that Itoman fishermen invented. OCVB's official Itoman–Tomigusuku gourmet course and Mapple both feature it.

dish: Gurukun (double-lined fusilier) sautéed in butter-soy, with island-vegetable sides such as house soy-milk tofu, served on yachimun and Ryukyu glass
n: Do~me Gohan Café, Ryukyu Glass Village, Itoman (土～夢ごはんカフェ)
address: 169 Fukuchi, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan (Ryukyu Glass Village)
w: The café beside the glass-blowing workshop at Ryukyu Glass Village, serving meat and fish mains — notably butter-soy gurukun, Okinawa's prefectural fish — with island-vegetable side dishes on local pottery and Ryukyu glass. JAL's Skyward crew picks recommend it and Stripes Okinawa reviewed it.

dish: Terrace-grilled chicken teriyaki plate in house sauce; homemade cakes from the showcase
n: Cafe Lodge, Tamagusuku Kakihana, Nanjō (カフェ ロッジ)
w: A two-storey mountain-lodge café (formerly CAFE Fūju) on a green hill above Kakihana Hījā spring, where every seat is upstairs looking through the trees to the southern sea. OCVB, the Nanjō City tourism association and Okinawa Traveler all list it among the area's view cafés; its teriyaki-chicken plate and daily cakes are the draws.

dish: Itoman-grown produce — the city's specialty carrots and mangoes among 120-130 local vegetables — plus handmade onigiri and sweets
n: JA Farmers Market Itoman Umanchu Ichiba, Michi-no-Eki Itoman (ファーマーズマーケットいとまん うまんちゅ市場)
address: Nishizaki-chō, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan (inside Michi-no-Eki Itoman)
w: Opened in November 2002 inside Michi-no-Eki Itoman, it is one of Okinawa's largest farm stands, with 1,000+ contracted growers and the highest footfall of the prefecture's ten JA farmers markets — Okinawa Times reported it passing 16 million visitors, and Ryukyu Shimpo covered its 10-millionth. OCVB's official Itoman gourmet course recommends its handmade onigiri, sweets and tropical fruit.
